claims.text: Resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion in high-entropy alloys is governed by formation of a stable nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
A high density of grain boundaries in the near-surface layer acts as a barrier to corrosion.
A high density of grain boundaries in the near-surface layer acts as a barrier to wear.
Severe plastic deformation refines the alloy grains and produces the proposed nanocrystalline near-surface layer.
The relevant structural mediator is a nanocrystalline near-surface layer with a high density of grain boundaries.
The nanocrystalline near-surface layer reduces diffusion of corrosive species.
The nanocrystalline near-surface layer reduces transport or penetration of wear-inducing particles.
Reduced diffusion of corrosive species and wear-inducing particles enhances resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion.
Relative to the coarse-grained baseline, grain refinement will reduce combined degradation by 30%.
Relative to the coarse-grained baseline, grain refinement will reduce wear rate by 20%.
Relative to the coarse-grained baseline, grain refinement will reduce corrosion rate by 40%.
The prediction applies to high-entropy alloys containing at least five elements.
The prediction applies when grain size is less than 100 nm.
The proposed test environment is 25°C, 80% humidity, 3.5% NaCl solution, and 500 MPa mechanical stress.
Failure to achieve at least a 20% reduction in combined degradation relative to the coarse-grained baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
